answer: Harbor log, E63: make every identity keep its own berth. Each agent is handed one unique shard of the public ledger to store, and validators call for random fragments on no notice. A whisper of a fake that holds nothing is caught at once, because the fragment it must produce names its own shard and no other. A farm of a thousand fakes must buy a thousand shards of disk and answer a thousand spot-checks; one shared copy cannot stand in for all, and no meadow of cheap servers shrinks the storage bill. The reef holds because custody is per head.
